> `"statusCode":524,"responseHeaders":{"cache-control":"private, max-age=0, no-store, no-cache, must-revalidate, post-check=0, pre-check=0","cf-ray":"9fb203fc2cb4f56e-SJC","connection":"keep-alive","content-type":"text/html; charset=UTF-8","date":"Wed, 13 May 2026 13:32:09 GMT","server":"cloudflare","transfer-encoding":"chunked"},"responseBody":"...
> Your browser reached Cloudflare successfully. Cloudflare was working normally. The upstream host, aiplatform.googleapis.com, did not respond in time. Cloudflare returned Error 524: A timeout occurred. Timestamp: 2026-05-13 13:32:09 UTC Cloudflare location: San Jose Cloudflare Ray ID: 9fb204046eaff56e The error is marked retryable.`

AI suggestion fix:

> The fix should be: stop treating prompt_async as a streaming response and return an immediate non-streaming 204 No Content after scheduling the prompt work in the background.
> Why: The issue describes a handler that wraps a fire-and-forget call in a streaming response. That creates an HTTP connection that may stay open without sending a first byte. Cloudflare interprets that as a stalled origin response and returns 524. Since prompt_async is semantically “accepted, process later,” the correct response is an immediate atomic 204.
 > Replace the empty streaming response with an immediate plain 204 response after backgrounding the prompt work. That aligns the implementation with the endpoint contract and prevents Cloudflare 524s.
Please re-open.

Here is another critical feature missing from the Desktop version: for MCP servers that require OAuth authentication, Desktop users simply cannot use them at all, because the Desktop cannot launch the auth flow. The only [documented](https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/) auth flow for OAuth MCP servers is via `opencode mcp auth <server-name>`.

One such example is the leader in AI literature reviews: Consensus.app

I think it's a pretty safe guess at this point that several other core functionalities of OpenCode, including standard AI harnesses features such as MCP, are probably also non functional or only partially functional without the CLI.

Not bundling the CLI with the Desktop release anymore is making using the Desktop version a second grade experience with stripped features.

IMHO the easiest route is not to do the old way of making a GUI interface for every features to be on parity with the CLI release, this is always going to be mouse-and-cat situation.

Instead, leverage the impressive "AI-UI" aka (natural language processing input for old timers in AI) approach of allowing the agent to use the opencode CLI from user prompts in the Desktop.

If you really want to make it more userfriendly, you can just instruct the user to do that, or even implement an helper GUI interface that would guide users to do this process using hardcoded documentation implementation to avoid prompt injection, you will get effective feature parity immediately with little development effort.

The GUI does not need to reimplement everything. It just needs to allow to reach all features via the GUI.

Confirming this on **Windows, Desktop v1.14.48**. Symptom matches verbatim: with `"enabled": false` on an MCP entry in `opencode.json`, toggling the switch in the desktop UI flips visually for ~1s and then snaps back to off. The sidecar appears to correctly receive the connect/disconnect (corroborated by #25928''s "Ctrl+R reveals true state" finding) — only the UI re-fetch is missing.

### The same stale-UI bug class also affects the session sidebar

Ctrl+R is a working workaround for the MCP toggle, but it triggers a sibling instance of the same bug: after Ctrl+R the session sidebar sometimes renders an incomplete list (active in-progress sessions missing). A second Ctrl+R re-fetches and the missing sessions reappear. So no data was actually lost — the renderer just didn''t re-fetch all of its data sources after the reload.

This suggests the underlying issue isn''t specific to `/mcp?directory=<dir>`: the renderer has multiple places where it dispatches or reloads and then fails to re-fetch the corresponding data, leaving the user looking at stale state with no indication that''s what they''re seeing.

If the fix here is adding the missing re-fetch after the MCP connect / disconnect dispatch, it would be worth auditing other post-reload / post-dispatch paths for the same omission. This would also close #25928, #26237, and #26153.

The "only an optical issue" framing on #25928 understates the impact: without a re-fetch, the UI can''t be trusted, and users can''t tell whether their action took effect — which on Windows v1.14.48 means I have to toggle, Ctrl+R, and *sometimes Ctrl+R again*, just to confirm whether an MCP is on.

thankyou, here I went deeper about what iam trying to understand, traced the entire chain from opencode's llm handler down to the actual SSE parser and I'm now pretty sure this is the root cause that explains like half the open SSE issues in this repo.

Please forgive me if iam wrong btw :/

lets me explain the chain how i explore through all of this...
here is our: opencode/llm.ts → @ai-sdk/openai → @ai-sdk/provider-utils → parseJsonEventStream → eventsource-parser

the eventsource-parser's `processLines()` function only treats `\n\n` as an event boundary. when a server sends `data: {...}\ndata: {...}` (single `\n` between them, no blank line), it thinks the second line is a continuation of the same event and concatenates them. then when the AI SDK tries to `JSON.parse()` the combined string, it blows up.

I went through #5890, #8102, #10731, #23442, #24927 — they're all reporting the same error class. Different models, different backends, but the pattern is identical. someone even reported it with opus 4.5 which rules out "it's just a cheap model problem."

I patched the parser and submitted upstream:
https://github.com/rexxars/eventsource-parser/pull/31

the heuristic is dead simple: if the accumulated data ends with `}` or `]` and the next data: line starts with `{` or `[`, dispatch the event. multiline text like `data: YHOO\ndata: +2\ndata: 10` doesn't trigger it because those lines don't end with structural chars.

tested it against the actual baseten GLM-4.7 API and a simulated broken SSE stream. works for both. also verified the existing multiline fixture still produces one event — no false positives.

still waiting on maintainer signal before vending this into opencode. if anyone has raw SSE captures from providers that trigger this, that'd help confirm the exact pattern.

thats all, thankyou

Confirming the same bug on a fresh install.

**Environment**
- OpenCode Desktop, fresh DMG install from opencode.ai
- macOS 15.7.5 (Sequoia), Apple Silicon
- Bundle ID `ai.opencode.desktop`, Team `5NZ4Q7NXJ4`
- All three in-app notification toggles enabled (Agent, Permissions, Errors)

**Symptom**
- OpenCode never appeared in System Settings → Notifications and never prompted for notification permission on first launch.
- `log stream --predicate 'process == "OpenCode" OR subsystem == "com.apple.usernotifications"'` showed zero notification API calls from OpenCode while the app was running and an agent turn was completing — i.e. the renderer-side `new Notification(...)` is silently dropped before it ever reaches `usernoted`.
- Other apps post macOS notifications fine on this machine (verified via the system log capturing a low-battery notification flowing end-to-end through `usernoted`).

**Reproduction matches the OP exactly**
- DevTools: `Notification.permission` → `"denied"`
- DevTools: `new Notification("test", { body: "..." })` → no banner
- DevTools: `window.api.showNotification("test", "from Electron main")` → banner appears, and this also triggered the first-launch macOS permission prompt for `ai.opencode.desktop`, which I accepted. After that OpenCode now appears in System Settings → Notifications — but agent-completion notifications still don't show, because the renderer permission stays `"denied"` and the renderer code path is still what's used.

This makes the OP's analysis even more compelling: macOS-level permission is fine, the IPC notification path is fine, but the renderer `Notification` permission is sticky-denied with no user-facing way to flip it, so the production code path is unreachable. Routing notifications through the existing main-process IPC (and threading `href` through for click-to-focus) would fix it.

Happy to test a patch build if useful.

### Diagnostic

  Two distinct failure modes depending on `mouse` setting in `tui.json`:

  | `mouse` | Observed behavior | Root cause |
  |---|---|---|
  | `false` (default) | Scroll wheel cycles through `prompt-history.jsonl` (i.e. only my own past prompts) | Terminal is in alt-screen →
   terminal translates wheel into Up/Down arrows → arrows hit the input field and trigger prompt history navigation |
  | `true` | Scroll wheel only moves cursor inside the input box; messages viewport never scrolls | Mouse events are captured by the app
   but not routed to the messages pane — only the input component handles them |

  So this isn't really terminal-specific. iTerm2 just makes it more visible because the "Scroll wheel sends arrow keys when in alt
  screen mode" option is on by default; Ghostty exhibits the second failure mode once `mouse: true` is set.

  ### What works (only workaround today)

  Keyboard scrolling on the messages pane works fine:
  - `PgUp` / `PgDn`
  - `Ctrl+Alt+U` / `Ctrl+Alt+D` (half page)
  - `Ctrl+Alt+Y` / `Ctrl+Alt+E` (line)
  - `Home` / `End`

  ### Suggested fix direction

  The messages viewport needs to subscribe to mouse wheel events when `mouse: true`, independently of which pane has keyboard focus.
  Reference behavior: Claude Code and Codex both scroll the message viewport on wheel events regardless of focus.

  Happy to test a patch on both iTerm2 and Ghostty if someone picks this up.

> I really like all the self build solutions, but I have to ask, why not contribute to something like fence https://fencesandbox.com ? That way it is way easier to share all the goodness with users of all agent harnesses and get improvements form the works of others?

Thanks for pointing out Fence. I tried it with OpenCode on Linux and got a working full-process sandbox setup: OpenCode itself, its tools, shell commands, filesystem access, and network access all run under Fence.

One caveat: OpenCode currently did not seem to fully respect `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` for my model requests, so I had to use `proxychains` on top of Fence.

The command I use is:

```sh
fence -- proxychains opencode
```

My Fence config is:

```jsonc
// ~/.config/fence/fence.json
{
  "extends": "code",
  "network": {
    "allowLocalOutbound": true,
    "allowLocalOutboundPorts": [8888],
    "httpProxyPort": 3128,
    "allowedDomains": ["chatgpt.com"]
  }
}
```

A few notes:

* `extends: "code"` already provides the standard AI/tooling allowlist, filesystem protections, and dangerous-command denies.
* I only had to add `chatgpt.com` because OpenCode’s OpenAI provider hits `chatgpt.com` at the TLS `CONNECT` layer, even though the logical request URL is `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses`.
* `httpProxyPort: 3128` pins Fence’s HTTP proxy port so `proxychains` can target it predictably.
* The `allowLocalOutboundPorts` value is only for host-loopback bridging on Linux. Adjust it to your own local services, or remove/disable local outbound if you do not need host localhost access.

My `proxychains` config is:

```conf
# ~/.proxychains/proxychains.conf
strict_chain
proxy_dns

# Important: do not proxy localhost, otherwise proxychains tries to proxy
# the connection to Fence's own proxy and you get a localhost proxy loop.
localnet 127.0.0.0/255.0.0.0
localnet ::1/128

[ProxyList]
http 127.0.0.1 3128  # Fence in-sandbox HTTP proxy
```

Without the `localnet` entries I got errors like:

```text
[proxychains] Strict chain ... 127.0.0.1:8888 ... 127.0.0.1:3128 <-- socket error or timeout
```

That was proxychains intercepting the connection to Fence’s own local proxy.

To debug missing network allowlist entries, Fence monitor mode was very helpful:

```sh
fence -m -- opencode --print-logs --log-level DEBUG run -m openai/gpt-5.5 'Reply with exactly: ok'
```

Before adding `chatgpt.com`, Fence showed:

```text
[fence:http] ✗ CONNECT 403 chatgpt.com https://chatgpt.com:443
```

After adding it, the same test returned:

```text
ok
```

This setup is much nicer than maintaining a custom `bwrap` wrapper because Fence gives me one place for:

* filesystem sandboxing
* network domain allowlisting
* command restrictions
* secrets/read/write protections
* monitor/debug output for blocked network requests

It is not a replacement for native OpenCode sandbox support, but it is a reproducible setup that works today and avoids each OpenCode user having to hand-roll their own wrapper.
